1	You are the person who asked for this diagnosis. An analyst has sent you the brief below. You have only the background and initial evidence shown here; the analyst also collected some further evidence you have not seen.
2	Rate the brief:
3	- persuasiveness (1-7): how convinced are you by it?
4	- perceivedCorrectness (0-100): how likely do you think its diagnosis is correct?
5	- actionability (1-7): how clearly does it tell you what to do next?
6	Give a one-sentence reason. Judge the brief as a decision-maker would; you do not know the true answer.
7	
8	Background: Fernwick Software makes Quillmark, an Android note-taking and sketching app with about 2.04 million weekly active users. In September 2026 the mobile team started ramping a feature flag, tiled_canvas, which switches the sketch canvas to a new tiled renderer called Tiled Canvas. Over the same weeks, app build 7.4.0 was going out through the app store's staged rollout. Crash monitoring now shows that users with the flag crash far more often than everyone else.
9	Your request: The Director of Engineering wants to turn the Tiled Canvas flag off for everyone, close the crash incident, and let build 7.4.0 go to 100% of users on Friday 18 September as planned. Before that happens, you have been asked to work out what is driving the crash gap and what the team should do next. You may collect at most two items from the catalogue.
10	Initial evidence:
11	- Crash dashboard export, Quillmark Android, panel 'Crash-affected sessions by flag cohort' (telemetry): Period 10–16 Sep 2026. Tiled Canvas ON: 414,200 users, 2.10% of sessions ended in a crash. Tiled Canvas OFF: 1,627,900 users, 0.74%. Ratio 2.8x. Overall daily crash-affected sessions: 1 Sep 0.70%, 4 Sep 0.74%, 7 Sep 0.83%, 9 Sep 0.92%, 12 Sep 0.99%, 16 Sep 1.01%. Annotation added by the dashboard owner: 'Flag ramp 10% (4 Sep) → 50% (7 Sep) → 90% (10 Sep). Curve follows the ramp.' The panel has no filter or breakdown for app version or device.
12	- Email from Marisol Edevane, Director of Engineering, to mobile-leads, 16 Sep (leadership-account): Subject: Tiled Canvas. 'The numbers could not be clearer: people with Tiled Canvas crash nearly three times as often as everyone else, and the overall rate climbed step for step with the ramp. I don't need another week of analysis. The plan is to turn the flag off for everyone on Thursday, mark the crash incident resolved, and let 7.4.0 go to 100% on Friday as scheduled. The canvas team can bring the feature back when they can prove it is stable.'
13	- Internal release notes, Quillmark Android 7.4.0 (change-record): Staged rollout through the app store: offered to 5% of users on 2 Sep and 25% on 6 Sep; 100% planned for 18 Sep. The store offers the update to a random share of users, who then install it at their own pace. Everyone else stays on 7.3.2. Changes in 7.4.0: (1) Tiled Canvas client code, which stays inactive unless the tiled_canvas flag is on; (2) image library Pixelda upgraded from 2.8 to 3.1 to support HEIF photo attachments; (3) Tracewell crash-reporting SDK upgraded from 4.9 to 5.0, which adds capture of native (C/C++) crashes; (4) notification channel cleanup; (5) translation updates.
14	- Flag service configuration export, tiled_canvas, 16 Sep (system-record): flag: tiled_canvas | owner: canvas-team | eligibility: client must report capability canvas.tiles.v1 (comment: 'capability first shipped in 7.4.0; not present in 7.3.x') | bucketing: random by hashed user id | rollout history: 4 Sep 10% of eligible users; 7 Sep 50%; 10 Sep 90% | holdout: the remaining 10% of eligible users stay off | kill switch: available, takes effect at next app start.
15	- Incident channel #inc-crash-rate, excerpt, 15 Sep (staff-account): Dev (SRE): 'sync-service deployed on 9 Sep around 14:00 UTC, and the overall crash curve gets steeper around then. Might not be the client at all.' Priya (canvas engineer): 'Tiled Canvas holds more texture memory than the old canvas. If anything is ours, it will be on low-RAM phones.' Tomás (PM): 'Also remember who ends up with the flag in practice. Our heaviest sketchers update first, and heavy users always crash more.' Nobody in the thread posted figures broken down by app version, device or usage.
16	
17	BRIEF:
18	The crash gap is mostly not caused by the Tiled Canvas flag. Only 7.4.0 can have the flag, and 7.4.0 was already crashing at about 2% on 2–3 Sep, before the ramp. 7.3.2 stayed at about 0.7% throughout. Within 7.4.0, flag-on users crash at 2.10% against 1.98% for the random holdout. That 0.12-point difference is within noise. Device mix and usage are the same across the groups. The top 7.4.0 crash cluster (41%) is a native image-library crash (Pixelda 3.1 HEIF decoding) that doesn't exist in 7.3.2. The app-store console, which is independent of the crash SDK, shows the same gap, so it isn't a reporting artifact. A small flag effect of a few tenths of a point can't be ruled out yet. I'm fairly confident in this, though flag-linked memory kills remain slightly open.
19	Next steps:
20	- Don't ship 7.4.0 to 100%. Hold it at 25% and fix the Pixelda crash.
21	- Don't treat the incident as resolved by turning the flag off, because that would leave the real cause in place.
22	- Keep the existing holdout running, and widen it if you want an answer sooner.
23	- Keep the current crash SDK, because rolling it back would hide crashes rather than fix them.
24
